title: Horns Pick & Roll
description: Pick-and-roll run from the Horns alignment — two screeners at the elbows, endless options either side.
whatIsIt: Horns is an alignment: the ball handler up top, two bigs at the elbows (the 'horns'), and two wings in the corners. The horns pick-and-roll is a ball screen set by either elbow big, with the other big available as a second screener, a pop threat, or a dive man.

Its power is symmetry. The defense doesn't know which side the screen is coming from, and after the first screen, the second big can re-screen, slip, or space. It is a play call that contains multitudes.
Horns PNR is a favorite late-game and ATO call because it is simple to run but hard to guard — the same look produces a drive, a roll, a pop, or a second-side action.
whyItMatters: Most PNR attacks come from one predictable spot. Horns gives you two screeners, two sides, and built-in counters without changing the call. For coaches, it is maximum optionality from minimum teaching; for players, it is a read-based action that rewards IQ.

howTo.title: Set the Horns alignment
howTo.detail: Ball up top, bigs at the elbows, wings in the corners. Spacing must be exact — the elbows are the launch pads.

howTo.title: Choose the screen side
howTo.detail: Either big sets the ball screen. Go to the side with the weaker on-ball defender or the slower big.

howTo.title: Use the second big
howTo.detail: After the first screen, the opposite big can re-screen (double drag look), dive to the rim, or pop. This is what separates Horns from a plain PNR.

howTo.title: Read the coverage
howTo.detail: Same reads as any PNR — over, under, drop, switch — but now with a second screener as the release valve when the first action is covered.

howTo.title: Flow to the weak side
howTo.detail: If the first side is walled off, swing the ball and run the other horn. The defense just shifted; attack the new gap.

coachingPoints: Teach the alignment first — bad Horns spacing (bigs too low or too wide) ruins every option.
Give the ball handler freedom to choose the side; called sides become predictable.
Drill the second-big reads separately: re-screen, dive, and pop are three different skills.
Wings must stay in the corners until the action develops — early drifting lets help arrive.
commonMistakes: Running the screen with the wrong big for the matchup — always attack the weaker side.
The second big standing and watching instead of re-screening or spacing.
Forcing the first side when the defense has clearly loaded up on it.
gameSituations: ATO plays and late-game, when you need a reliable high-option action.
With two skilled bigs who can both screen and make decisions.
Against switching defenses — the second screener punishes the switch.
